title: SYMMETRY-REDUCED strict h=0 K=4 (4 identical agents) CRRA REE contour-Phi fixed-point study
status: core_complete (gamma=0.1 + Picard done & pushed; gamma=0.25/0.5/1.0 with Picard running in background, will append + push on completion)

task1_cython_port.operator_used_for_study: Numba phi_K4_halo (parallel=True, 4 threads) -- faster than the single-threaded Cython port; symmetry reduction is the main tractability win, so we use the faster operator. Cython port built + bit-exact validated.

validation.note: Cython kernel reproduces the Numba operator BIT-EXACTLY (0.0 diff) over the full 13^4 grid on the NL IC and a random P. Built with -O3, fastmath OFF (matches Numba fastmath=False).

speed.note: Cython is single-threaded; Numba uses prange over 4 cores. Cython matches exactly but is ~3.4x slower here, so the study uses the parallel Numba operator.

task2_symmetry.representation: sorted index tuples (multisets) i1<=i2<=i3<=i4 over the inner grid
task2_symmetry.note: Phi maps symmetric->symmetric BIT-EXACTLY (asymmetry of Phi(symmetric P) = 0.0, far below the 1e-12 target). The reduced phi_red = reduce(phi_full(expand(v))) is therefore exact; orbit-average vs representative-read agree to 4e-16.

interpretation_gamma_0.1.genuine_fixed_point: ONLY the fully-revealing point (FP0) is a true fixed point: ||F||inf = 9.45e-6 (NK floor ~1e-5), deficit = 1.1e-16, d_FR = 1.7e-10. P = lam(tau * sum_k u_k) essentially solves Phi(P)=P.
interpretation_gamma_0.1.naive_dedup_caveat: The dedup counts 5 'distinct' low-residual points, but FP1-FP4 (||F||inf = 0.0088, 0.067, 0.067, 0.087) are NOT fixed points -- they are where Newton-Krylov STALLED on the non-smooth residual. Treating ||F||inf<0.005 as the genuine-FP bar, there is exactly ONE equilibrium (FR).
interpretation_gamma_0.1.(a)_unique_PR_equilibrium: NO unique PR equilibrium. The unique genuine equilibrium at gamma=0.1 is FULLY-REVEALING (deficit ~0), NOT partially-revealing. This DIFFERS from K=3 (unique PR eq, deficit ~0.27). Adding a 4th identical agent appears to push the strict-h0 REE onto the FR manifold.
interpretation_gamma_0.1.(b)_nonsmooth_floor: YES, recurs strongly. Every non-FR seed (NL, constant, both random) stalls at ||F||inf ~ 0.07-0.20; NK cannot drive below. Even the FR point has a residual FLOOR ~1e-5 (NK cannot reach machine zero) due to the non-differentiable contour-crossing decisions -- the same active-set non-smoothness that capped K=3 at ~0.2. The K=4 stall band (~0.07-0.2 for off-FR seeds) is comparable to K=3's ~0.2.
interpretation_gamma_0.1.(c)_picard_period2_oscillation: NO. See picard_oscillation block: Picard from NL IC converges (deficit -> 0.0003, FR) with a small ~0.015 non-smooth ||F||inf plateau; no clean period-2 cycle. K=3's period-2 learning oscillation does NOT recur at K=4.
interpretation_gamma_0.1.summary_vs_K3: Of the three K=3 structural features, K=4 reproduces the NON-SMOOTH RESIDUAL FLOOR (b) but NOT the unique-PR-equilibrium (a, K=4 is FR instead) and NOT the period-2 Picard oscillation (c, K=4 converges to FR).

picard_oscillation.verdict: K=4 does NOT show the K=3 period-2 learning oscillation. Undamped Picard from the NL IC drives the revelation deficit to ~0.0003 (essentially fully revealing) within ~5 iters, while ||F||inf falls from 0.43 to a small NON-SMOOTH plateau ~0.012-0.020 (mean 0.0165) where it wobbles irregularly (NOT a clean 2-cycle: |P_t - P_(t-2)| ~0.04-0.05 stays comparable to ||F||inf). So a non-smooth residual floor recurs, but at ~0.015 (vs K=3's ~0.2) and the limit is FR, not a partially-revealing 2-cycle.
